title: Holika Dahan Outfit Ideas for the Bonfire Evening in 2027
excerpt: Holika Dahan outfit ideas for the bonfire puja abroad: natural fabrics near the fire, a pinned dupatta, warm shawls and festive kurta sets.
body:
For Holika Dahan, wear a natural-fabric kurta set in cotton or chanderi, keep your dupatta pinned close to your body, and add a warm shawl for the evening chill. It is a puja first, so choose something festive yet practical, and save your colour-play clothes for the next morning.

This guide is for women abroad attending a Holika Dahan bonfire at a temple, a community ground or a family backyard, often on a cold March evening. A [grey hand block print cotton kurta set with Kota Doria dupatta](/products/grey-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-kota-doria-dupatta-set/) is exactly the kind of look we have in mind.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Our block prints are hand printed by karigars, and our pieces are made in our own Jaipur unit.*

## What do people wear to Holika Dahan?

Holika Dahan is the bonfire evening before the day of colours. Families gather around the fire, offer prayers, walk around it in parikrama and share sweets. Holi falls in late March 2027 (check your local calendar), and the bonfire is lit on the evening before colour play.

Because it is a puja, most women wear a neat kurta set or a simple suit rather than the old clothes they plan to play in. Think of it as a festive evening outfit with practical edges: easy to stand in, easy to walk in around the fire, and warm enough for an outdoor gathering after sunset.

Colour is your choice. Bright festive shades such as red, yellow, orange, pink and green are popular, but soft greys and pastels with a printed or embroidered detail look just as graceful in firelight.

## Which fabrics make sense near a bonfire?

The most important rule is simple: avoid synthetic fabrics close to the fire. Polyester, nylon and many shiny blends can melt with heat, while cotton and silk-cotton chanderi are more sensible choices. Whatever you wear, keep a respectful distance from the flames and keep an eye on children.

| Fabric | Near the fire | Feel on a cold evening | Our view |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block print cotton | Sensible choice | Light, needs a layer | Best everyday pick |
| Chanderi | Sensible choice | Light with a soft sheen | Best for a dressier puja |
| Kota Doria dupatta | Keep it pinned | Airy and sheer | Lovely, but drape it close |
| Georgette or chiffon | Keep well back | Floaty, often synthetic | Better for indoor events |
| Polyester blends | Avoid | Can feel clammy | Skip for the bonfire |

## How should you wear your dupatta around the fire?

A loose dupatta and an open fire do not mix. The breeze around a bonfire is unpredictable, and the ends of a long dupatta can swing out further than you think while you walk in parikrama.

Pin it on one shoulder and let it fall down your back, or wrap it across the body and tuck the end at your waist. If your family covers the head during prayers, drape it over your head and secure it with a small pin at the shoulder. On a very windy night, it is perfectly fine to leave the dupatta at home and wear a shawl instead.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Kota Doria is an open, airy weave that drapes beautifully but moves with every breeze. For a bonfire evening, fold it lengthwise and pin it at the shoulder so it sits close. Chanderi has a soft sheen that looks lovely in firelight without the stiffness of heavier silks, which makes it easy to wear for a long evening outdoors.

## How do you stay warm at an outdoor Holika Dahan in March?

In the UK, Canada and the northern US, a March evening can feel properly wintry once the sun goes down. In Australia it is early autumn and usually mild, and in the UAE the evenings are pleasant. Dress for where you are.

For cold cities, wear thermal leggings under your pants or palazzos and a fitted long-sleeve thermal under your kurta. Choose a kurta with a little ease so the layer does not show. Finish with a shawl wrapped close, closed shoes and a coat you can slip off near the warmth of the gathering.

Pack these before you leave:

- A warm shawl or wrap
- Two small safety pins for your dupatta
- Closed, flat shoes for uneven ground
- Your phone light for the walk back to the car
- Any puja items your host has asked you to bring

## Frequently asked questions

**What colour should I wear for Holika Dahan?**
There is no fixed rule. Bright festive colours are popular, and many families prefer to avoid all-black for a puja, so ask your host if you are unsure.

**Can I wear my Holi play clothes to Holika Dahan?**
You can, but most people dress a little nicer for the bonfire puja and keep their play clothes for the next morning.

**Is it okay to wear a dupatta near the bonfire?**
Yes, as long as it is pinned or wrapped close to your body. If the wind is strong, swap it for a shawl.
